target.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT sar.timestamp AS time, 'M2AD anomaly — score ' || ROUND(sar.anomaly_score::numeric, 2) || ', ' || COALESCE(sar.details->>'severity', 'unknown') AS text FROM sensor_anomaly_results sar WHERE sar.detector = 'm2ad' AND sar.is_anomaly = true AND $__timeFilter(sar.timestamp) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Anomaly Episodes — when and how strong
panels.description: One point per detection interval in which M2AD flagged the sensor vector. The stored score is 1 − p-value and only intervals with p < 0.1 are persisted, so every event sits above ~0.9 by construction — a rising floor, not a rising fault. Red vertical markers (dashboard annotation) mark the same events on every panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT sar.timestamp AS time, MAX(sar.anomaly_score) AS "anomaly score" FROM sensor_anomaly_results sar WHERE sar.is_anomaly = true AND sar.detector = ANY(string_to_array(NULLIF('${detector:csv}', ''), ',')) AND ('$run_id' = '' OR sar.run_id = '$run_id') AND $__timeFilter(sar.timestamp) GROUP BY sar.timestamp ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Anomaly Frequency — how often
panels.description: Detections per time bucket. Clusters of bars are sustained anomaly episodes; isolated bars are single-interval spikes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('minute', sar.timestamp) AS time, COUNT(DISTINCT sar.timestamp) AS "detections" FROM sensor_anomaly_results sar WHERE sar.is_anomaly = true AND sar.detector = ANY(string_to_array(NULLIF('${detector:csv}', ''), ',')) AND ('$run_id' = '' OR sar.run_id = '$run_id') AND $__timeFilter(sar.timestamp) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Anomaly Detail — what happened (per channel)
panels.description: M2AD scores the whole channel vector jointly, so the same score is written for every channel at that instant; this table shows the raw reading each channel carried when the episode fired, plus the computed severity. A channel whose reading is far from its normal band is the likely contributor.

targets.rawSql: SELECT sar.timestamp, sar.source_id AS channel, ROUND(sar.anomaly_score::numeric, 3) AS score, sar.details->>'severity' AS severity, sar.details->>'zone' AS zone, sar.value AS reading FROM sensor_anomaly_results sar WHERE sar.is_anomaly = true AND sar.detector = ANY(string_to_array(NULLIF('${detector:csv}', ''), ',')) AND ('$run_id' = '' OR sar.run_id = '$run_id') AND $__timeFilter(sar.timestamp) ORDER BY sar.timestamp DESC, sar.source_id LIMIT 500

panels.title: Detector Activity
panels.description: How much each detector has run and how its scores are distributed. `detection_runs` counts distinct runs, `anomalous_rows` counts per-channel rows (8 channels are written per flagged interval).

targets.rawSql: SELECT sar.detector, COUNT(DISTINCT sar.run_id) AS detection_runs, COUNT(*) AS anomalous_rows, ROUND(AVG(sar.anomaly_score)::numeric, 3) AS avg_score, ROUND(MAX(sar.anomaly_score)::numeric, 3) AS max_score, MAX(sar.timestamp) AS last_detection FROM sensor_anomaly_results sar WHERE sar.detector = ANY(string_to_array(NULLIF('${detector:csv}', ''), ',')) GROUP BY sar.detector ORDER BY sar.detector

panels.title: Recent Alerts
panels.description: Every alert the detector wrote — sensor-only and fused (sensor + camera) — across all zones. `message` names the contributing score(s).

targets.rawSql: SELECT a.timestamp, a.source_id, a.alert_type, a.severity, a.score, a.message FROM alerts a WHERE $__timeFilter(a.timestamp) ORDER BY a.timestamp DESC LIMIT 100

list.name: run_id
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT run_id FROM sensor_anomaly_results ORDER BY run_id DESC LIMIT 20

list.name: detector
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT detector FROM sensor_anomaly_results ORDER BY detector
